incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT detected: runtime-prod GPU paging surge. Affected fleet: gpu-pool-7. Error spike observed in inference runtime (OOM / fragment paging). Auto-escalating to on-call.

miguel (oncall): I’m on it. Putting full triage hat on. Any customer-facing impact yet?

jun (support): Saw 502s for customers on shard-7 for ~3m, CS opened two tickets but no major SLA breach yet. Notifying enterprise customers.

raj (runtime): grabbing allocator + slab stats now. Hypothesis: sudden KV cache growth + increased batch concurrency causing fragmentation/pagewalks.

emily (sre): Can you paste recent pmap/top output and dmesg OOM logs? Also what changed in prod deploys in last 30m?

raj (runtime): logs: ```
GPU0 / gpu-pool-7: free_mem 1.2GB -> 120MB over 6m
KVCache entries: 5.1M -> 8.9M
active_batches: 64 -> 192
rpc_latency p50 12ms -> 40ms
OOM messages: "out of memory while allocating 512MB" repeated
```

sara (infra): No infra deploys in last hour. Some traffic pattern spike from customer X (L7): long-context chat sessions increased seq length avg 2.3x. Could explain KV growth.

nora (mlops): Model-side change: nothing pushed. But traffic weighting changed via load-shedding rule update 45m ago (lower priority fallbacks removed). Might have allowed heavier models to hit runtime more.

miguel (oncall): Quick mitigation plan: 1) reduce max_batch_size on pool-7 to 8 (from 32) 2) enable kvcache-eviction aggressive policy 3) route ~30% traffic to warm fallback region us-west-2. Can someone run commands?

raj (runtime): Applying batch-size tweak now: ```/ops/prodctl set-config --pool gpu-pool-7 --max-batch-size 8``` Rolling this to 10% first. Watching memory.

emily (sre): I’ll flip eviction policy to aggressive: ```/ops/kvctl set --pool gpu-pool-7 --eviction-policy aggressive --target-free-mb 800``` Doing a canary on 4 nodes.

jun (support): Noted. Informing customers that we're investigating and throttling heavy sessions to reduce errors.

(3m later) raj (runtime): Canary nodes show free_mem recovering 1.5GB -> 3.8GB, KV entries down ~40%. No new OOMs on canary. Latency p50 back to ~16ms.

miguel (oncall): Good. Roll the batch-size and eviction policy to remaining nodes. Start traffic reroute too. Notify if any regressions.

nora (mlops): Long-term hypothesis thread: sequence-length driven KV growth caused fragmentation due to high concurrent batches. Potential fixes: prompt-length/gating at edge, dynamic kv admission, kv compaction, or per-model kv size caps. Adding to backlog.

emily (sre): For RCA notes: collect full allocator traces (cuda memstats), slab histograms, and per-request kv delta. Raj, can you dump nvprof/cuda-memstats and upload to shared logs?

raj (runtime): Uploading artifacts: /artifacts/3615000000/cuda-memstats.txt and /artifacts/3615000000/kv-deltas.log. Key snippet: ```
allocator histogram: small-alloc buckets spiked at 8-64KB
fragmentation index: 0.62 -> 0.82
pagewalks/sec: 120 -> 980
```

miguel (oncall): Customer impact summary for postmortem: short 3–7m error spike affecting ~12% of requests to shard-7, primary root cause: KV cache growth + increased concurrent batching exposing allocator fragmentation -> transient OOMs. Immediate mitigation: reduce batch size, aggressive eviction, route traffic.

jun (support): CS updated customers and logged two tickets as P1-provisionally. No billing credits yet; awaiting RCA.

nora (mlops): Next steps: 1) add a traffic-based trigger to auto-reduce batch-size when per-gpu free memory < 1GB 2) implement KV admission cap per-request 3) run scheduled defrag/compaction during low-traffic windows.

emily (sre): Scheduling follow-up postmortem 0900 UTC tomorrow. Please attach logs and hypothesis checklist to the incident ticket. Marking incident resolved for now. :white_check_mark: 

miguel (oncall): Thanks team. If anything resurfaces re-open thread. Leaving a short timeline in the ticket from logs. :eyes:
